data_section_full_text:
3.1 Sample construction


Our primary dataset is an index of earnings-related news articles prepared by AP
between Jan.1, 2012, and Nov. 12, 2015. Automated articles appear in our index as
early as July 2014, but AP went through several months of testing before it began
distributing automated articles. AP’s index does not identify whether an article was
distributed, so we ensure that each article was made available to the public by matching
each article from the index to content on Yahoo. Yahoo automatically republishes 100%
of the earnings announcement articles received over AP’s newsfeed, and we find that
the automated articles appear on Yahoo starting Oct. 13, 2014. AP’s other members and
newsfeed customers also had access to the automated articles beginning on Oct. 13,
2014. Thus we define automated articles before this date as undistributed, and we
exclude them from our sample.

We use data from Compustat, CRSP, Zacks, IBES, and Wall Street Horizon to
construct a sample of firms’ quarterly earnings announcements over the same period as

E. Blankespoor et al.


the AP index. Our basic sample requirements are that the firm-quarter has sufficient
data to identify the earnings announcement date, earnings surprise, and abnormal stock
returns over trading days [0, +2] relative to the earnings announcement. We exclude
trusts, closed-end funds, and REITs. To minimize sample noise, we require that each
earnings announcement date per Compustat is the same as the date provided by Zacks,
IBES, or Wall Street Horizon (deHaan et al. 2015). We use timestamps from Wall Street
Horizon and IBES to identify after-hours announcements and set day 0 to the following
trading day for market tests. We also require that each firm have at least one available
observation in the sample both before and after AP began distributing automated
articles. As detailed in Panel A of Table 1, our available sample for analysis consists
of 60,566 firm-quarters for 4,292 unique firms.

We merge the AP index and our sample of earnings announcements to identify
whether each firm received AP coverage within days [0, +2], relative to the
earnings announcement date. Our initial merge is based on company tickers and
names provided in the AP index. In instances where the AP index contains no
company identifiers or when the AP identifiers do not match to any firm in
Compustat/CRSP, we match based on company names mentioned in the article’s
headline. We can match roughly 84% of the AP index articles to Compustat/CRSP.
Most of the unmatched articles do not have any identifying company information,
relate to foreign firms, or are earnings-related but occur outside days [0, 2] of the
earnings announcement window (e.g., articles about monthly sales reports, an
unbundled forecast, or an upcoming earnings announcement).

Once automated firm coverage is initiated, the firm typically receives automated articles in all future quarters. Of the 4,292 available firms, 11.2% have one
quarter of missing automated coverage after initiation, and 5.7% have two or more
missing quarters. While many missed stories are due to technical bugs that are
unrelated to the content of the firm’s earnings announcement, other missed stories
are potentially concentrated among firms that experience unusual events requiring
human intervention. (Stock splits, for example, can cause errors for the algorithm
in comparing EPS to prior periods or the analyst consensus.) <sup>9</sup> AP typically does
not retroactively report on earnings announcements, so an automated article will
not be distributed if workers cannot resolve technical bugs and quality control
failures within a day or two of the earnings announcement. We therefore expect
that missed articles are most likely to occur on days with many earnings announcements. Because we cannot specifically identify why an automated story is
missed, we drop 246 firms missing automated articles in more than one quarter
following their robo-journalism initiation. For the 480 firms with one missed
quarter, we keep the firm but drop the quarter missing coverage.
